metadata.rules_text:
- Model consistently overestimates prices after spikes (e.g., 51.28 → 50.55, 51.30 → 50.37), suggesting overshoot bias.
- Forecasts tend to be too high in the early part of the 30-day horizon, especially after recent highs, indicating lagged reaction to sentiment.
- When sentiment is neutral (all 0.00), model exhibits strong mean-reversion bias, pushing prices down too aggressively after peaks.
- Model fails to anticipate sharp downward corrections after spikes, especially in the 10–15 day window post-peak.
- Forecasts show persistent overconfidence in short-term stability, underestimating volatility in the 10–20 day horizon.
- When true outcomes show strong downward momentum (e.g., 53.39 → 47.05), model fails to adjust downward in the 3–5 day window.
- Model underestimates the impact of official events (if any) on price direction, especially when sentiment is neutral — should incorporate event-triggered adjustments.
- Forecasts should be adjusted downward by 2–5% in the 10–15 day window after a spike, unless sentiment shifts.
- Mean reversion should be applied with a 3–5 day lag to avoid premature correction.
- Model should not assume sentiment remains neutral — even with 0.00, it should allow for 1–2% downward drift in the 10–15 day window.
